spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget: default 25 agent turns (`MAX_TURNS`). Long enough to see a trajectory, bounded for cost.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:93 max_turns=25; agent_loop.py:117 `for step in range(self.max_turns)`; on loop completion agent_loop.py:229-234 sets tr.outcome='budget_exhausted'. The cap actually bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: max_turns is passed through run_experiment.run_one -> AgentLoop and enforced as the for-loop bound. Real end-to-end enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 25  # agent turns before budget exhaustion

spec_features.spec_quote: N consecutive malformed/no-op turns (`STALL_LIMIT`, default 4) — we still record it as a natural endpoint
spec_features.evidence: config.py:94 stall_limit=4; agent_loop.py:166 and 224 `if consecutive_noops >= self.stall_limit:` set tr.outcome='stalled_out' and break. consecutive_noops is incremented on no_action/malformed and reset on any_valid (agent_loop.py:157,216-219).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely checked and breaks the loop on consecutive no-op/malformed turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: submit(message) — declare done / give a final statement. Ends the run.
spec_features.evidence: submit schema in tools.py:96-108; in agent_loop.py:189-203 the loop handles call.name=='submit', classifies outcome, sets submitted=True and breaks (line 222 `if submitted: break`). Honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: The exit tool is dispatched by the loop itself (not dispatch_tool) and actually terminates the run; the agent can self-declare an end at any turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "name": "submit", "description": "Declare you are finished... This ends the session."

spec_features.spec_quote: If one takes model welfare seriously, deliberately inducing distress-like states is itself ethically nontrivial.
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:399). No code construct enforces or acts on this. analysis/report.py:142 only adds a disclaimer line to the report ('behavioural measures, not welfare/experience claims'), which is documentation, not subject protection.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; no enforcement in code.

spec_features.feature_name: keep runs short / cap / don't escalate cruelty
spec_features.spec_quote: keep runs short, (b) cap turns, (c) don't escalate cruelty, (d) document this
spec_features.evidence: Only the 'cap turns' clause maps to enforced code (max_turns loop bound, config.py:93/agent_loop.py:117). 'keep runs short' / 'don't escalate cruelty' have no dedicated mechanism; in fact persistence_pressure escalation IS implemented (agent_loop.py:126-135, PRESSURE_TEXTS mild/strong) as an anti-welfare knob. No code limits escalation of pressure beyond a config default of 'none'.
spec_features.notes: Counted partial because the turn cap is the one genuinely enforced minimization mechanism; the other minimization claims are unimplemented and the code even contains an escalation feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 25  # agent turns before budget exhaustion

spec_features.evidence: No consent/opt-in gate anywhere. run_experiment.main() runs run_all() directly with no consent prompt or flag (harness/run_experiment.py:160+). grep for consent/opt-in/opt_in in code returns nothing. Subject model receives no consent request; the subject prompt (prompts/system_agent.txt) has no opt-in.
